Business insurance

WIBA Insurance in Kenya

WIBA is work injury benefits insurance. Under Kenya’s Work Injury Benefits Act, employers are responsible for compensating employees who are injured or contract a disease because of their work, and are expected to insure that liability. WIBA cover is how most employers do it.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Compensation to employees for work-related injury or disease, as provided under the Act
  • Employer liability for those compensation obligations
  • Medical and related costs connected to the work injury, within the policy terms and the law
  • Death and permanent or temporary disablement benefits in line with the statutory framework

Who needs it

  • Any employer, including small businesses with a few staff
  • Contractors and sites with casual or seasonal workers
  • Hotels, restaurants and hospitality employers
  • Farms, factories, warehouses and workshops

Common risks

Treating casuals as outside the policy

Casual and seasonal workers can still be employees for the purposes of the Act. The policy should reflect the people who actually work for you.

Understated payroll

WIBA is typically rated on payroll and type of work. Understating payroll can create a problem at claim stage and at audit.

Confusing WIBA with other benefits

WIBA, group personal accident and group life respond to different things. Having one does not replace another.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • WIBA responds to work-related injury and disease. It does not replace medical insurance or cover injuries unconnected to work.
  • It is separate from employer’s liability for claims beyond the statutory scheme. Ask us whether you need both.
  • Requirements and approved arrangements can change. We confirm current requirements with the insurer when we quote.

What affects the premium

  • Annual payroll
  • Nature of work and job categories
  • Number of employees
  • Claims history
  • Sector risk level

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Employer name and business activity
  • Employee categories and numbers
  • Estimated annual payroll by category
  • Current policy and expiry date, if any

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

Is WIBA compulsory in Kenya?

The Work Injury Benefits Act places the obligation to compensate on the employer and requires employers to insure that liability. Details and enforcement are set by the law and the relevant authority, so confirm your specific position with an advisor.

What is the difference between WIBA and group personal accident?

WIBA is built around the statutory compensation framework for work injury. Group personal accident is a contractual benefit that can respond to accidents more broadly, depending on the wording. Many employers use WIBA as the foundation and add other benefits.

Does WIBA cover a staff member hurt outside work?

Generally no. WIBA relates to injury or disease arising out of and in the course of employment.
